clue.text: Short shabby detective — US — I went there!

indicators.note: a short word is cut down: COLUMBO loses its last letter

parts.note: Columbo, the scruffy TV detective in the raincoat, cut short

explanation.surface: A breathless tourist's postcard boasting about visiting the home of a scruffy American TV detective.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer: Columbus could say of the US 'I went there!' The exclamation mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Columbus sailed to the Americas, so he might say of the US that he went there.

clue.text: Feuding family's pills laced with uranium

indicators.note: the pills are laced with, so contain, the extra ingredient

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A poisoning plot: a family's medicine spiked with something radioactive.
explanation.walkthrough: The poisoned pills fit the Romeo and Juliet story, where potions and poison decide everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The Capulets are Juliet's family, locked in a feud with the Montagues.

clue.text: 'Animal star sign.' 'Chameleon?' 'Not entirely.'

indicators.note: only part of the word is used, so the answer sits inside it

parts.note: the three letters sit in the middle of the lizard's name, after CHAME

explanation.surface: A snatch of dialogue: someone asks which star sign is an animal, another suggests chameleon, and is told 'not quite'.
explanation.walkthrough: The quiz-show exchange is the disguise: 'Not entirely' reads as a verdict on the guess, but it tells you to take part of CHAMELEON.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo, the lion, is a sign of the zodiac named after an animal.

clue.text: Brief moments with that French woman — and wine

parts.note: mo is short for moment, as in 'half a mo'

explanation.surface: A romantic snatched interlude with a Frenchwoman over a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' simply joins the two pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Moselle is a white wine from the Moselle valley in Germany and Luxembourg.

clue.text: 'Undecorated'? Right to get rise, as base layer's been applied

indicators.note: the R (right) moves up the word, which in a down entry means earlier

parts.note: the word as printed, in quotation marks

explanation.surface: A decorator's note: a bare surface isn't really undecorated once the undercoat is on.
explanation.walkthrough: Not a free shuffle: only the R moves. In UNDECORATED it sits after UNDECO; lift it two places and you get UNDE-R-COATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something undercoated has had its base layer of paint put on.

clue.text: English: scratching head, unable to qualify

indicators.note: scratching out the head removes the first letter

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A pupil scratching their head over an English exam they can't pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching head' reads as puzzlement but means delete the first letter; E then takes the vanished U's place.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable someone is to qualify them, make them fit or able to do something.

clue.text: Amateur artist to capture rising waterfall

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: to gain is to capture or win

explanation.surface: A Sunday painter setting out to get a rushing waterfall onto canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: A, RA and GAIN make ARAGAIN, which reads upwards as NIAGARA.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara Falls is the famous waterfall on the US–Canada border.

clue.text: Great amounts rain heavily on blokes protecting duck

indicators.note: the blokes surround the duck
in a down entry, one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, O

explanation.surface: Men sheltering a duck from a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' pretends to be the bird sheltering from the rain; in cricket it is a score of nothing, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British measure: a bucketload is as much as a bucket holds, so bucketloads means plenty.

clue.text: In placid manner, pick six characters from seven lycanthropes

indicators.note: take six letters running straight through the words that follow

parts.note: start after the S of seven and run across the word break for six letters

explanation.surface: Calmly choosing six out of a line-up of seven werewolves.
explanation.walkthrough: The six characters sound like werewolves to pick, but they are letters. A lycanthrope is a werewolf.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak evenly is to speak calmly, in a placid manner.

clue.text: Edward by island on sailboat, reversing at water's edge

indicators.note: the whole string is read backwards
the island comes before the sailboat
'by' in the sense of 'beside', so Edward stands next to the island

parts.note: a sloop is a single-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: Edward sailing a small boat past an island, turning back near the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: ED, I and SLOOP make EDISLOOP, which reads backwards as POOLSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Poolside means beside a pool, at the water's edge.

clue.text: Awkward, grand and long — at the outset, uncle's hosted

indicators.note: take the first letter of uncle

parts.note: to long for is to ache for

explanation.surface: An uncle playing host to someone clumsy, grand and tall.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes into ACHE to make AUCHE, with G in front. 'long' looks like an adjective but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauche means socially awkward or clumsy.

clue.text: Everyman is improperly described by two lines making damaging accusation

indicators.note: to describe is also to draw round, so the lines enclose the middle

parts.note: the setter is I, and 'I be' is ungrammatical for 'I am'

explanation.surface: A complaint that the setter has been misrepresented in a couple of lines of print.
explanation.walkthrough: Everyman is the setter, so 'Everyman is' becomes I + BE, the improper form of 'I am'. 'described' means drawn around: L-IBE-L.
explanation.definitionFit: A libel is a published false statement that damages someone's reputation.

clue.text: Ones drawing fictional pig? They appeal to the girls

parts.note: Babe is the sheep-herding pig of the novel and film

explanation.surface: Something that attracts a famous fictional pig turns out to be irresistible to women.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, magnets for Babe are things that draw the pig. The question mark marks the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe magnets is slang for men, or things like flash cars, that attract women.

clue.text: Squeeze a beauty, we're told, to arouse memories

indicators.note: what we hear rather than what is written

parts.note: wring = squeeze; a belle is a beauty

explanation.surface: Hugging an old flame to jog the memory.
explanation.walkthrough: WRING and RING, BELLE and BELL sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: When something rings a bell, it stirs a faint memory.

clue.text: What the absent-minded (or uncaring) greengrocer does

definitions.text: What the absent-minded (or uncaring) greengrocer does

parts.note: the literal reading: a forgetful shopkeeper fails to hand over one piece of fruit
the idiomatic reading: someone who could not care less

explanation.surface: A fruit seller who forgets part of your order.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed '(or uncaring)' points to the idiom, while the greengrocer makes it literal.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a fig stands for something worthless, so to withhold even that is to be utterly indifferent.

clue.text: Postpone unit's dance and indoor game

parts.note: in US usage, to table a motion is to postpone it
a foot is a unit of length
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A military unit putting off its dance and playing a game indoors instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unit' suggests soldiers, but it is the measurement. Table football is the game with rods of little players, also called foosball.
explanation.definitionFit: Table football is a tabletop game played indoors.

clue.text: Doesn't leave out trendy crosswords' building blocks: about 500!

indicators.note: the clues go round the 500

parts.note: a crossword is built from clues

explanation.surface: A fashionable crossword-lover insisting on about 500 clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about 500' reads as an estimate of how many clues, but it places the Roman numeral inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by negation: the opposite of excluding, so 'doesn't leave out' is a plain synonym phrase.

clue.text: Range of human inaction unsettling

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that people's idleness is disturbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' reads as scope, as in the range of human behaviour, but it is a line of mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the geographical sense: a range is a connected line of peaks.

clue.text: Upriver, glimpsed along Nile's drainage area: national, primarily?

definitions.text: Upriver, glimpsed along Nile's drainage area: national, primarily?

indicators.note: in the first place, so each word gives its first letter

parts.words: Upriver, glimpsed along Nile's drainage area: national
parts.note: seven words, each contributing its first letter

explanation.surface: A traveller spotting someone upstream in the Nile basin and guessing their nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: Uganda lies upriver in the Nile's drainage basin, and its national is a Ugandan.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda contains the Nile's upper reaches, so a national glimpsed there would be Ugandan.

clue.text: Relate to sorrow

definitions.meaning: a verb: to be about or have a bearing on something
a noun: worry or distress on someone's behalf

explanation.walkthrough: 'Relate to' suggests empathising with someone's sorrow, but it means 'be about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Concern means both to be about something and a feeling of worry or distress.

clue.text: Literary figure found meandering in Detroit, mostly

indicators.note: wandering letters, rearranged
most of the word but not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A literary celebrity spotted wandering around Detroit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literary figure' suggests an author or a character, but an editor works in literature too.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a figure in the literary world, preparing others' writing for print.

clue.text: On track, bat's simple stroke

indicators.note: the track comes first, placed on the bat

parts.note: to dog someone is to track them
a table-tennis bat is also called a paddle

explanation.surface: A cricketer on track, praising a batsman's easy shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bat' and 'stroke' suggest cricket, but the stroke is a swimming one.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog paddle is the simplest swimming stroke, paddling like a dog.

clue.text: Nosy astronauts left

parts.note: NASA is the US space agency, employer of astronauts

explanation.surface: Inquisitive astronauts have left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nosy' looks like prying but means 'of the nose'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means relating to the nose, which is nosy in a literal sense.

clue.text: Studious, tense and wimpish

explanation.surface: A portrait of a nervous, bookish weakling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' reads as anxious, fitting the wimp, but it is the grammatical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweedy describes the bookish, academic type in tweed jackets.

clue.text: Swayed, being camp

explanation.surface: Someone moving their hips theatrically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swayed' tempts as physical movement, but it means influenced.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected means both influenced and artificially showy.

clue.text: Stoves regularly seen in sets

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every second letter is taken

explanation.surface: Cookers routinely found in matched sets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets' suggests matching kitchen equipment, but it means television sets.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortening: 'set' alone has long meant a television or radio receiver, as in 'switch on the set'.

clue.text: Once again despatched gift without slightest hint of provocation

indicators.note: the gift goes without, that is lacks, the letter that follows
only the first letter of provocation

explanation.surface: Returning a present that was sent unprovoked.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is read as RE-SENT, not the verb 'resent', which the word 'provocation' hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-sent means dispatched once again.

clue.text: Suffers sea song I butchered

indicators.note: the letters are hacked about

explanation.surface: A singer apologising for mangling a sea shanty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffers' could be the listeners' reaction to the butchered song.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to suffer anguish.
